title: Normalized common-stage presentation of the ordinary Qbar exchange
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$ and an algebraic closure $\Omega/\mathbf Q_\ell$, and use the raw finite-stage coefficient categories [def-weil-pbc-qbar-category] and their scalar systems [def-weil-pbc-finite-stage-pair-category]. Let $X,X',Y,Y'$ be Noetherian finite-dimensional schemes on which $\ell$ is invertible, and let $s=(g',f',f,g)$ be a chosen Cartesian square [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square]. A normalized ordinary exchange presentation consists of: proofs that the actual completed operations $Rf_*,Rf'_*,Lg^*,Lg'^*$ preserve the integral constructible categories at every finite coefficient field [def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-complete], [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback]; four coherent exact scalar families [def-weil-pbc-descent-interfaces] whose stage functors are exactly the raw rationalizations of these four restricted operations; the canonical direct-image and pullback scalar-beta specifications, including at equal fields [def-per-rational-direct-image-family], [def-weil-pbc-descent-interfaces]; and a scalar-compatible family $\tau:Rf_*;Lg^*\to Lg'^*;Rf'_*$ whose component on every integral representative is exactly the localization of the actual completed exchange [def-exchange-projection]. Here semicolons denote application in order. No preservation, existence of such a presentation, or invertibility is asserted by this definition.

For arbitrary four coherent stage-system morphisms $F,G,H,J$ and a compatible stage transformation $\tau:F;G\to H;J$, define their descended exchange by $(F_{\mathrm{desc}};G_{\mathrm{desc}})\xrightarrow{c_{F,G}^{-1}}(F;G)_{\mathrm{desc}}\xrightarrow{\tau_{\mathrm{desc}}}(H;J)_{\mathrm{desc}}\xrightarrow{c_{H,J}}(H_{\mathrm{desc}};J_{\mathrm{desc}})$, where $c$ is the canonical stage-system composition comparison. For a pair $K=(E,K_E)$ and any $M\supset E$, define its representative to be the pair-category morphism class at $M$ of $\beta_{F;G,M/E}\,;\tau_{M,T_{M/E}K_E}\,;\beta_{H;J,M/E}^{-1}$. For a normalized ordinary presentation $P$, define $P.\mathrm{exchange}$ and $P.\mathrm{atStage}$ by these formulas for its four families and $\tau$. The case $M=E$ is included. These definitions retain all the actual operations, beta normalizations and exchange components and make no arbitrary choice of a natural transformation.
